title: Adaptive Console Topology: Lane-based Sidebar Partitioning & Route Rhythm
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a lane-based, progressively collapsing sidebar and route rhythm for the Redwood Console that prioritizes quick access to dashboards (cost, latency, rollouts) while preserving multi-workspace tenancy and fast workspace switching. The goal is to reduce cognitive load for power users, surface rollout controls and cost lenses earlier in flows, and provide layout patterns that map directly to A/B rollout states and Dedicated/Private product modes.
goals: Make core console surfaces (Overview, Models, Dedicated, Rollouts, Cost) reachable within 2 clicks from any workspace context
Provide a compact lane mode for dense screens (developer dashboards) and an expanded lane for discovery/onboarding
Ensure route stability during workspace switch and allow pinned cross-workspace dashboards
Expose rollout controls (canary, A/B, fallback) inline with model routes
Improve discoverability of cost breakdowns and token-level traces without adding new top-level items
decisions: Adopt a three-tier lane model: Primary (core product areas), Contextual (workspace-specific tools and dashboards), Utility (account/settings, support).
Use progressive collapsing: full lane -> icon+badge lane -> micro icon rail depending on container width and user preference.
Workspace switching becomes modal-less: persistent quick-chip at top of Primary lane, with in-place context swap to avoid full route reloads where possible.
Route rhythm aligns resource URLs to lane hierarchy (e.g., /workspace/:id/primary/:route, /workspace/:id/context/:tool), enabling predictable deep links for dashboards and rollouts.
Rollouts controls will surface a compact summary card in the Contextual lane with a CTA to open a focused rollout panel; full rollout orchestration stays in a separate route for advanced ops.
Accessibility: keyboard-first navigation, explicit focus zones per lane, and ARIA landmarks to support screen readers.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates progressive collapse across three breakpoints (desktop, laptop, tablet) and preserves access to top 5 routes within 2 clicks.
Workspace switch completes without full page reload in prototype and preserves last-opened contextual panel when toggling workspaces.
Rollouts summary card shows current canaries, last 24h error delta, and quick promote/rollback buttons that open the detailed rollout pane.
Performance benchmark: lane collapse/expand animations run at 60fps on target dev machines (M1/M2 equivalent) with no layout thrash.
Keyboard navigation test cases (tab/shift-tab, arrow navigation, space/enter activation) documented and passing in the prototype demo.
Design tokens and spacing scale documented for engineering handoff (tokens referenced in spec).
tasks: Finalize Figma screens for three breakpoints and annotate interactive states
Run 2x round of guerilla usability testing with 6 engineers/PMs (task-based scenarios)
Sync with frontend: define CSS/JS contract for progressive collapse and route rhythm
Create storybook components for Primary/Contextual/Utility lanes
Add instrumentation hooks for analytics (clicks to rollouts, cost dashboard opens, workspace switch time)
Prepare handoff deck for PMs, Eng, and Solutions (20–30 minute walkthrough)
Open engineering ticket bundle (ENG-xxxx) for implementation and link rollout API contract
